A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, we propose the first inference model to infer user location from the spatial distribution of check ins and photos; we evaluate existing LPPMs with the proposed inference method and show that existing LPPMs are not effective; and finally we propose a novel dummy mechanism, photo check, to defend against inference attack.

, the privacy of a user in LBSN is vulnerable to the spatial distribution of historical events, and a LPPM that considers the spatiotempora correlation of check ins and photos is necessary to protect user's location privacy.

, in a location based social network, the privacy of user's location can be breached through spatiotemporally analyzing multiple events including check ins and photos and that, the existing LPPMs are not effective to defend against this attack.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in LBSNs, user's location privacy is not only affected by his/her check ins, but also by the photos he/she shares, and that the privacy of user's check ins is not well protected by existing dummy mechanisms.
, in LBSNs, user's location privacy is not only influenced by the spatial correlation among user's check ins but also the temporal correlation between check ins and shared photos.
, in order to preserve location privacy in LBSNs, it is important to take the impact of photos on user's location privacy into account.
